text_solutions.text:
"A. Question:
In which of the following reactions does increasing pressure not increase the yield of products?
B. Given Data:
  • Reaction 1: 2SO2(g) + O2(g) ⇌ 2SO3(g)
  • Reaction 2: NH4HS(s) ⇌ NH3(g) + H2S(g)
  • Reaction 3: N2O4(g) ⇌ 2NO2(g)
C. Concept:
  • Le Chatelier's Principle: When a system at equilibrium is subjected to stress, the system will shift in a direction that tends to counteract the stress and re-establish equilibrium.
  • Effect of Pressure:
    • Increasing pressure favors the side of the reaction with fewer moles of gas.
D. Mathematical Calculation:
1. Analyze each reaction:
  • Reaction 1: 3 moles of gas on the left, 2 moles of gas on the right. Increasing pressure will shift the equilibrium to the right (towards products).
  • Reaction 2: 0 moles of gas on the left, 2 moles of gas on the right. Increasing pressure will shift the equilibrium to the left (towards reactants).
  • Reaction 3: 1 mole of gas on the left, 2 moles of gas on the right. Increasing pressure will shift the equilibrium to the left (towards reactants).
E. Final Answer:
2. NH4HS(s) ⇌ NH3(g) + H2S(g) and
3. N2O4(g) ⇌ 2NO2(g)
In both reactions 2 and 3, increasing pressure will not increase the yield of products."
